newsitem.title: USA: U.S Army lowers standard, raises bonuses for recruits.
newsitem.headline: U.S Army lowers standard, raises bonuses for recruits.

text.p: The Army said Tuesday it was lowering recruiting standards slightly and raising bonuses to make up for losses to a good civilian job market and in some cases to sex harassment publicity.

Lt. Gen. Frederick Vollrath told reporters a requirement for high school graduates has been dropped to 90 percent of all recruits from the previous 95 percent and said the bonus budget has been more than trebled to $44 million this year.

Vollrath, Army deputy chief of staff for personnel, said the top enlistment bonus has been raised to $12,000 from the previous $8,000. He said very few combat specialists will get the full $12,000 and many recruits get no bonus because they are based on how much the Army needs particular skills.

The general said the Army needs more incentives for recruits primarily because a good civilian economy is giving more young people jobs just when post-Cold War up and down adjustments have created a recruit shortage.
But Maj. Gen. Alfonso Lenhardt said recruiting may also have been hurt slightly by the scandal in which several Army drill sergeants have been charged with rape or sex harassment of women trainees.

Lenhardt, commander of the U.S. Army Recruiting Command, said 25 of the 6,000 women in a delayed enlistment programme dropped out because of the sex harassment allegations and recruitment of women dipped a tenth of one percent this year.
